summary: This is a well‑executed, preregistered paired confirmatory study that applies a verifier‑grounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline to intent→configuration NetOps tasks in a Mininet emulation. The experimental preregistration, execution artifacts, deterministic validator traces, and analysis outputs are thorough and appear internally consistent. The main result (baseline 196/200, guarded 200/200; n10=4, n01=0; paired risk difference 0.02; exact McNemar p=0.125) is reported cautiously and bounded within the study’s emulation scope. The paper is reproducible given the archived artifacts and includes the required Disclosure Statement and master‑prompt provenance.
critical_issues: Inconsistent uncertainty reporting: the manuscript reports an exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.125 (non‑significant) yet also reports a paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.005, 0.04] that excludes zero. These two statements are contradictory under standard frequentist interpretation and must be reconciled (see Required Revisions).

References formatting: the manuscript's cited_record_ids / reference list appears to rely on DOI/arXiv identifiers only. The References section must present conventional IEEE‑style bibliographic entries (authors, title, venue, year) for every cited record when that metadata is available.

Provider/condition accounting ambiguity: provider_call_audit shows stage_counts {shared_initial_generation:200, repair:4} and condition_counts {shared:200, guarded:4}, yet the execution manifest and paired counts indicate 200 guarded episodes were completed. The manuscript must clarify the model‑call accounting and the meaning of 'condition_counts' vs episode counts so readers can reconcile 400 completed episodes with 204 model calls and the stated stage/condition counts.
required_revisions: Reconcile and correct the uncertainty reporting: (a) recompute and/or reframe the paired CI so it is statistically consistent with the exact McNemar test (or explicitly explain why the bootstrap percentile CI may be unreliable here and present an alternative exact CI method); (b) make all uncertainty statements internally consistent (do not claim both 'p>0.05' and a CI that excludes zero without justification). Use only analysis artifacts already archived (bootstrap seeds/resamples and paired outcome table) — no new data collection is requested.

Replace identifier‑only reference entries with full IEEE‑style bibliographic references (authors, title, venue, year) for every cited record where such metadata exists. Ensure each numbered citation in text maps to a conventional bibliographic entry in the References section.

Clarify model‑call and condition accounting in Methods and Results: explicitly explain shared_initial_candidate semantics, show how model_calls_used=204 arises from 200 shared initial generations + 4 repairs, and resolve the apparent mismatch between 'condition_counts' = {shared:200, guarded:4} and completed_episode_count=400. Update any prose that could be read as implying the baseline and guarded arms received different initial model generations (they did not). Provide a brief deterministic accounting paragraph or table using artifacts already in the bundle (e.g., provider_call_audit and execution summary hashes).
optional_revisions: Report per‑vendor/template subgroup contingency tables and descriptive effect sizes from the archived results (explicitly labeled exploratory) to help readers assess heterogeneity across strata.

Discuss limitations of the deterministic validator more concretely by summarizing representative classes of semantic violations that the validator cannot detect (with examples from archived failure traces) and how such blind spots could affect external validity.

Replace or augment the bootstrap percentile CI with one or more alternative interval estimators for small discordant counts (e.g., exact conditional CI/Newcombe methods) and briefly justify the chosen interval estimator using the archived analysis log.
